title: Calf as strong-God symbol like Apis attributes—Scripture still allows relative reference and gravest condemnation together
source_text: XLI. Nonnulli vero censent, nec omnino improbabiliter, Jeroboam in vitulis voluisse exprimere Jehovam, tanquam Deum fortem & potentem, cujus virtus bovis robore symbolice significaretur; quemadmodum Aegyptii in Apide quaedam numinis attributa mystice adumbrabant. Sed quicquid sit de ista conjectura, certum est ex Scriptura, cultum vitulis exhibitum ad Jehovam referri potuisse, & nihilominus gravissime damnari.
pass_a_gloss: But some judge, and not altogether improbably, that Jeroboam wished in the calves to express Jehovah, as a strong and powerful God, whose virtue would be symbolically signified by the strength of an ox; just as the Egyptians in Apis mystically shadowed certain attributes of the divinity. But whatever may be of that conjecture, it is certain from Scripture that the cult exhibited to the calves could be referred to Jehovah, and nevertheless be most gravely condemned.
pass_b_english: Optional reading: ox-strength as Jehovah’s power symbol, Apis-style attributes.
Either way Scripture holds together relative reference to Jehovah and gravest condemnation.

lemmas.gloss: by the strength of an ox

choices.why: Divine perfections symbolized, not alien gods.
